title: Label each character when it first appears
statement: When a picture or film introduces several people, make each visually distinct and label each with name and role on first appearance, as overlaid text, not narration alone.
detail: In review of a unit's opening film, a viewer found it hard to tell two of its characters apart. Inspection of the character frame found distinct figures but no visible name or role labels, consistent with that difficulty. The next illustrated version labelled the characters in the lesson, rather than putting a narrator character on screen.
against: One review comment and one inspected frame; the labelled version was built but never tried with students. Words and labels are kept out of generated images, so the labels have to be laid over the picture by the lesson or film. Props later carried part of the distinction without labels: "V14 (Cassio vs Iago) is now also carried by shot 15, where Cassio holds the lieutenant's order and Iago the banner." (`g9/library/text/L4224ba.txt`, line 32).
